pl-l4d42c3-d1e115.summary: Cites Pope Nicholas: one should love the one who lifted him from the font as a father; among spiritual siblings and children there is a free and holy communion, not consanguinity but spiritual nearness, so no lawful marriage can be made among them, since the laws do not permit marriage between natural and adopted children; if adoption forbids marriage, much more should those whom the Spirit's regeneration joins abstain from carnal union.
claims: Spiritual kinship forbids marriage among spiritual and natural children.
Spiritual kinship binds more than adoption.

pl-l4d42c3.summary: Nicholas holds that spiritual or adopted children cannot marry natural children: one should love the sponsor as a father; between spiritual siblings and children there is a holy communion called spiritual nearness, not consanguinity, so no lawful marriage can be made between them, as the laws forbid marriage between natural and adopted children; much more should those joined by the Spirit's regeneration abstain.
claims: Spiritual children may not marry the sponsor's natural children.
Spiritual kinship is stronger than adoption, which also impedes marriage.
